problem_statement: Estimate the risk of synthetic default within 90 days using information available when a request arrives. The score supports a simulated manual review queue.

notes.evidence: XGBoost led on Average Precision at 0.3338 versus 0.3258 for Logistic Regression. Logistic Regression led on ROC-AUC at 0.8213.
notes.limitation: The comparison was a single random split of operations, with 1,226 customers appearing on both sides. The AP difference was small and does not establish future performance.
notes.next_test: Compare on later applications with customer separation and a 90-day label-maturity gap. Check whether the AP advantage persists across periods.

exit_answers: Only 158 of 2,000 applications defaulted. AP focuses on the precision and recall of that rare class, which is the workload the review team cares about. ROC-AUC also captures how the score ranks classes overall.
Early stopping chooses a tree count using observed performance. The inner stopping split serves that purpose. Keeping the 2,000 comparison rows out of this choice preserves a separate estimate.
